borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
description: Conversion of existing dwelling into two flats (1 x 3 bed and 1 x 2 bed) including the construction of a front porch, a two storey front infill extension and a first floor rear and side extension with associated cycle and refuse storage
decision_conditions: The proposed development would result in the loss of a good quality family-sized dwellinghouse. This would be detrimental to the borough's stock of these type of dwellings, the identified local need for which is set out in the Development Plan and supporting evidence. The provision of two substandard units is not considered sufficient to justify this. The harm caused by way of a reduction in the borough's supply of this type of dwellinghouse significantly and demonstrably outweighs the benefits of the proposed flats. As such, the proposal would conflict with the following policies which seek to ensure that the borough's housing supply meets the needs of its residents:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December, 2024)Policies D6, H1, H2, H9 and H10 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SPDG 1, SP3 and DMH5 of The Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024)

In the absence of a parking stress survey with sufficient detail and evidence, officers are unable to determine whether the proposal would result in undue harm to the highway network. Further information is required on the proposed parking and the proposal fails to demonstrate whether sufficient car parking provision would be made or whether this could be adequately accommodated in the surrounding area. In the absence of such, the proposal is found to result in unacceptable parking stress and congestion in the vicinity of the application site.  As such, it fails to comply with the following policies:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December 2024)Policies T1 and T6.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September 2024)
